title: Earth's largest waterfall is hidden beneath the ocean
body: Between Greenland and Iceland, a huge underwater cascade flows through the **Denmark Strait**. Cold, dense water from the Nordic Seas sinks beneath warmer water and spills over a ridge in the seafloor. Gravity pulls this deep current down the slope, even though the whole scene is already underwater. NOAA describes it as Earth's largest waterfall.

slides.alt: Cross-section showing cold, dense water spilling over an underwater ridge and flowing beneath warmer water. Schematic, not to scale.
slides.caption: Water can flow downhill through other water when the two have different densities.

slides.heading: How an underwater fall works
items: Cold water approaches an underwater ridge.
The denser water sinks beneath warmer water.
It flows down the seafloor into the deep ocean.

slides.heading: Why you cannot watch it from shore
slides.text: This cascade is a submerged current. Its huge flow is hidden below the surface and is measured with scientific instruments.
